Pump for Stream A: Vapourtec R-series HPLC pump (KHU-PUMP-VAPOURTEC-R-SERIES) compatible with UV-150 system, 0.5 mL/min well within 0.01-10 mL/min range, max 42 bar >> 2.5 bar BPR back-pressure.

explanation:
# Flow Chemistry Design Brief: Two-Stage Photoredox Giese Addition / Aerobic Sulfoxidation

---

## (1) Proposed Flow Setup

**Reaction:** One-pot photoredox Giese radical addition of PMPSCH2TMS to acrylonitrile (Stage 1), followed by photosensitized aerobic sulfide-to-sulfoxide oxidation (Stage 2).

**Overall architecture:** Two sequential coil reactors connected in series via a T-junction for O₂ introduction. Single liquid pump feed; one gas MFC.

---

### Stage 1 — Anaerobic Photoredox Giese Addition

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Reactor | 10 mL PFA coil, 1.0 mm ID (KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML) |
| Light source | Vapourtec UV-150 with 450 nm module, 24 W, 355 mW/cm² |
| Temperature | 25.0 °C (UV-150 active cooling engaged) |
| Liquid flow rate | 0.42254 mL/min |
| Residence time | 7.1 min (inlet basis) |
| Atmosphere | Strictly anaerobic — pre-degassed feed only |
| Concentration | 0.1 M PMPSCH2TMS |

**Feed (Stream A):** Single pre-mixed, argon-degassed reservoir containing PMPSCH2TMS (0.1 M, 1.0 equiv), acrylonitrile (0.2 M, 2.0 equiv), and Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ (0.0005 M, 0.5 mol%) dissolved in EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer (5:1 v/v). Delivered by Vapourtec R-series HPLC pump.

---

### Inter-Stage Junction

At the outlet of Stage 1, a T-junction introduces O₂ gas (Stream B) via a Bronkhorst MFC at **0.947 sccm** (0.2981 mL/min actual at reactor conditions). This creates segmented gas-liquid Taylor flow entering Stage 2. The T-junction is the only point of O₂ contact with the process stream.

---

### Stage 2 — Aerobic Photosensitized Sulfoxidation

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Reactor | 9.7239 mL effective volume, FEP coil, 1.0 mm ID (KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML) |
| Light source | Manual blue strip LED, 448 nm, 62 mW/cm² (KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448) with fan |
| Temperature | 40 °C (fan-cooled manual photoreactor — fixed operating mode) |
| Liquid flow rate | 0.42254 mL/min |
| O₂ MFC | 0.947 sccm; gas holdup = 0.4137; gas/liquid ratio = 0.706 |
| Residence time | 7.1 min (inlet/STP apparent basis); 13.49 min in-channel (pressure-corrected) |
| BPR | 3.0 bar fixed BPR at system outlet |
| O₂ transfer sufficiency | 29.0× (mass transfer is not limiting) |

**Outlet:** Product stream (sulfoxide 4a in EtOH/buffer) collected after BPR for workup.

---

### Pre-Run Preparation

1. Sparge EtOH/pH 9 buffer (5:1 v/v) with argon for ≥20 min in a sealed reservoir.
2. Dissolve all reagents (PMPSCH2TMS, acrylonitrile, Ir photocatalyst) into the degassed solvent under argon; seal reservoir.
3. Purge all Stage 1 tubing and the PFA coil with degassed solvent before starting the reaction to displace residual air.

---

## (2) Why These Conditions Were Chosen

### Photocatalyst and Wavelength
Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)₂(dtbpy)PF₆ has its MLCT absorption tail extending to ~470 nm with a practical excitation maximum near 380 nm. The batch protocol uses 452 nm. The 450 nm UV-150 module is the closest available match. Three literature analogies support this choice:

- **Analogy 1** (Ir(ppy)₃ photoredox radical addition, MiChS flow photoreactor, 425 nm, 30 min residence time): confirms that Ir-photoredox radical Giese additions are feasible in flow at 20–30 min residence times with visible light. Chemically similar but uses fac-Ir(ppy)₃ in DMSO — our system uses a more oxidizing Ir(III) complex in EtOH/water.

- **Analogy 2** (Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]₂(dtbbpy)PF₆ photoredox cross-coupling, FEP segmented flow, 10 mL, 12 min, 440 nm): **same photocatalyst family**, confirms 12 min is sufficient at 50 °C in FEP tubing. Our 7.1 min at 25 °C with higher irradiance (355 mW/cm²) is consistent.

- **Analogy 3** (Ir(dFCF3ppy)₂(bpy)PF₆, Vapourtec UV-150, 10 mL PFA coil, 40 min at 0.25 mL/min, 450 nm): **most directly applicable** — identical reactor hardware and wavelength, same Ir catalyst class. Our higher flow rate (0.42254 mL/min vs 0.25 mL/min) and higher irradiance support a shorter residence time.

### Two-Stage Sequence

**Confidence: MEDIUM** — Best analogy score: 0.56. A related literature precedent was found but conditions differ. Validate key parameters (residence time, concentration) experimentally.

Final engineering validation: ready.

Final design disposition: SCREEN. No deterministic hard-feasibility conflict was found. Treat the design as a first experimental screen until wet-lab evidence validates it.

Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.

Substrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv
Michael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv
Photocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%

Concentration: 0.1 M
Scale: 0.2 mmol

Step 1 - Giese radical addition:
The reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free
conditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 deg C for
4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a
in 92% yield.

Step 2 - Aerobic oxidation:
After Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was
continued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 deg C for another
6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.

Total batch reaction time: 10 hours
Final isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%

Critical requirements:
- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.
- Air/O2 is introduced only after Step 1 is complete.
- Light and the photocatalyst are essential.
- The pH 9 buffer suppresses formation of the PMPSCH3 byproduct.

Reaction: One-pot photoredox Giese addition followed by aerobic oxidation.

Substrate/radical precursor: PMPSCH2TMS (1a), 0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv
Michael acceptor: Acrylonitrile (2a), 2.0 equiv
Photocatalyst: Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6, 0.5 mol%
Solvent: EtOH/pH 9 aqueous buffer, 5:1 v/v
Concentration: 0.1 M
Scale: 0.2 mmol

Step 1 - Giese radical addition:
The reaction mixture was maintained under argon under strictly oxygen-free
conditions. It was irradiated using a 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 deg C for
4 hours in a sealed pressure tube. This produced sulfide intermediate 3a
in 92% yield.

Step 2 - Aerobic oxidation:
After Step 1, the reaction vessel was opened to air. Irradiation was
continued using the same 10 W, 452 nm blue LED at 25 deg C for another
6 hours. The sulfide intermediate was oxidized to sulfoxide 4a.

Total batch reaction time: 10 hours
Final isolated yield of sulfoxide 4a: 95%

Critical requirements:
- Oxygen must be excluded during Step 1.
- Air/O2 is introduced only after Step 1 is complete.
- Light and the photocatalyst are essential.
- The pH 9 buffer suppresses formation of the PMPSCH3 byproduct.
Produce one executable two-stage continuous-flow design using only the frozen KHU inventory, preserving oxygen exclusion in Stage 1 and introducing air or oxygen only between Stage 1 and Stage 2.

_analogies.summary: This photoredox catalysis process involves a radical addition followed by oxidation using fac-[Ir(ppy)3] as the photocatalyst with 425 nm LED irradiation. The reaction was performed in DMSO solvent at 25°C using a MiChS flow photoreactor L-1 (M) with 2 mm ID quartz tubing and a 2.7 mL reactor volume. The flow process achieved a remarkable 30-minute residence time at 0.09 mL/min flow rate, compared to 24 hours required in batch conditions. Flow chemistry provided dramatic improvements with a 48-fold reduction in reaction time (from 24 hours to 30 minutes) and a substantial increase in yield from 22% in batch to 75% in flow. The enhanced performance in flow resulted from improved light penetration and better mass transfer in the thin quartz tubing, enabling more efficient photocatalytic activation and faster reaction kinetics.

pre_council_proposal.chemistry_notes: Two-stage continuous flow design. Stage 1 (anaerobic Giese radical addition): Stream A flows through KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML (10 mL PFA coil, 1 mm ID) irradiated by KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450 (450 nm, 24 W, 355 mW/cm2) in Vapourtec UV-150. PFA is transparent to visible light and rated to 80 C and 34 bar. UV-150 with additional cooling operates at 25 C (within 10-35 C additional cooling range). Stage 2 (aerobic sulfide-to-sulfoxide oxidation): O2 introduced via Bronkhorst MFC at T-junction after Stage 1 outlet; segmented gas-liquid Taylor flow enters KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML (20 mL FEP coil, 1 mm ID) irradiated by KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448 (448 nm, 62 mW/cm2) in KHU manual photoreactor with fan (40 C). FEP is transparent to visible light. The 40 C operating temperature for Stage 2 is slightly above the 25 C batch but acceptable and may accelerate oxidation. Incompatible pair O2 + alpha-thio radical is strictly separated by stage sequencing. Residence time basis for Stage 2 is inlet/STP apparent (gas-liquid system). Stage 1 residence time: 10 mL / 0.5 mL/min = 20 min (liquid-only, single phase). Stage 2 inlet residence time: 20 mL / (0.5 + 1.223) mL/min = 11.6 min apparent; in-channel (pressure-corrected at 2.5 bar abs, 40 C): gas volume compressed ~2.5x, so Q_gas_actual ~0.49 mL/min, t_in_channel = 20 / (0.5 + 0.49) = ~20.2 min. Total system residence time ~40 min vs 10 h batch (15x intensification). Analogies 1, 2, 3 all confirm 12-40 min residence times for Ir-photoredox in flow with 450 nm LEDs. BPR 2.5 bar selected as closest available above the 3.0 bar engineering recommendation; 7 bar available as fallback. Pump for Stream A: Vapourtec R-series HPLC pump (KHU-PUMP-VAPOURTEC-R-SERIES) compatible with UV-150 system, 0.5 mL/min well within 0.01-10 mL/min range, max 42 bar >> 2.5 bar BPR back-pressure.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Stage 1: V=10 mL / Q=0.5 mL/min = 20 min (liquid-only calculation). Engineering calc range 9.5-150 min; 20 min is within range. Analogy 3 (Vapourtec UV-150, same Ir photocatalyst class, 450 nm, 10 mL): 40 min at 0.25 mL/min — our higher flow rate (0.5 mL/min) gives 20 min, consistent with higher photon flux (355 mW/cm2 vs analogy's unspecified). Analogy 1: 30 min for Ir photoredox radical addition in flow. Analogy 2: 12 min for Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2 cross-coupling. 20 min is a reasonable starting point between analogies.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_basis: Stage 1 is single-phase liquid: basis = liquid-only V/Q. Stage 2 is gas-liquid: O2 equivalents based on inlet/STP MFC flow (1.12 sccm = 1.223 mL/min STP); pressure-corrected in-channel time reported separately as ~20.2 min at 2.5 bar abs.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_inlet_min: Stage 2: 20 mL / (0.5 + 1.223) mL/min = 11.6 min. Gas-liquid system; inlet/STP basis per universal physics rules.
reasoning_per_field.residence_time_in_channel_min: Stage 2: at 2.5 bar abs and 40 C, O2 gas compressed ~2.5x relative to STP, Q_gas_actual ~0.49 mL/min; t_in_channel = 20 / (0.5 + 0.49) = 20.2 min.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Engineering calculation: Q_total = 0.500 mL/min (liquid). Consistent with Analogy 3 (0.25 mL/min for 10 mL reactor) scaled to 10 mL Stage 1 at 20 min. Vapourtec R-series pump range 0.01-10 mL/min; 0.5 mL/min well within range.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Stage 1: 25 C per batch protocol and Chemistry Plan. UV-150 additional cooling mode supports 10-35 C; 25 C achievable. Stage 2: 40 C (KHU manual photoreactor with fan — only available temperature mode). Chemistry Plan notes 40 C is unlikely detrimental and may accelerate oxidation.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: Engineering calc: BPR required at 3.0 bar (gas-liquid system). Available fixed BPRs: 1.5, 2.5, 7.0, 8.0, 16.0 bar. 2.5 bar (KHU-BPR-FIXED-2P5BAR) is closest available above minimum needed to suppress degassing; 7 bar available as fallback if 2.5 bar insufficient. EtOH bp=78 C >> 40 C operating temp so solvent boiling not the driver; BPR is for gas-liquid flow stability.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: PFA for Stage 1 (UV-150 compatible, transparent to 450 nm, rated 80 C/34 bar, KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML). FEP for Stage 2 (manual photoreactor, transparent to 448 nm, rated 50 C/34 bar, KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML; 40 C operation is within 50 C max). Both materials are fluoropolymers compatible with EtOH/aqueous buffer. Analogy 2 used FEP tubing for Ir photoredox in flow.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.1 M per batch protocol and Chemistry Plan stream_logic. Analogy 2 used 0.05 M; our 0.1 M is within normal photoredox range. No adjustment needed.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Stage 1: KHU-REACTOR-PFA-1MM-10ML (10 mL) — matches Analogy 3 (Vapourtec UV-150, 10 mL) and UV-150 maximum coil volume limit (10 mL per hard constraints). Stage 2: KHU-REACTOR-FEP-1MM-20ML (20 mL) — largest available FEP coil for manual photoreactor; accommodates longer Stage 2 residence time needed for aerobic oxidation (batch ratio Stage2/Stage1 = 6h/4h = 1.5x; 20 mL vs 10 mL = 2x, conservative). Total 30 mL within manual photoreactor 30 mL capacity limit.
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: Stage 1: KHU-LIGHT-UV150-450 (450 nm measured, 24 W, 355 mW/cm2) — exact match to Chemistry Plan recommended_wavelength_nm=450 nm and Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy)PF6 MLCT absorption. Analogy 3 used identical UV-150 450 nm module. Stage 2: KHU-LIGHT-MANUAL-BLUE-448 (448 nm, 62 mW/cm2) — within Ir photocatalyst absorption envelope; only available flow photoreactor light source compatible with >10 mL coil. Chemistry Plan explicitly recommends this for Stage 2.
reasoning_per_field.wavelength_nm: 450 nm per Chemistry Plan recommended_wavelength_nm and batch protocol (452 nm). UV-150 450 nm module measured at exactly 450 nm. Stage 2 uses 448 nm (manual photoreactor) — within 2 nm of optimum, acceptable.
reasoning_per_field.deoxygenation_method: Hard constraint: no inline degasser permitted. Allowed method: pre-degassed solvent offline with argon sparging in sealed reservoir. Chemistry Plan deoxygenation_reasoning confirms this approach. Stage 1 tubing purged with degassed solvent before run.

literature_analogies: Analogy 1: Ir(ppy)3 photoredox radical addition, MiChS flow photoreactor, 30 min residence time, 425 nm — chemically similar (Ir photoredox radical addition); difference: fac-Ir(ppy)3 vs our Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbpy), DMSO vs EtOH/buffer, 2 mm quartz vs 1 mm PFA; adjustment: our higher irradiance (355 vs unspecified) supports shorter or similar residence time

Analogy 2: Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photoredox cross-coupling, FEP segmented flow, 10 mL, 12 min, 440 nm — same photocatalyst family (identical Ir complex); difference: cross-coupling vs radical addition/oxidation, DMF vs EtOH/buffer, 50 C vs 25 C; adjustment: our 20 min at 25 C is conservative relative to their 12 min at 50 C

Analogy 3: Ir(dFCF3ppy)2(bpy)PF6 photoredox, Vapourtec UV-150, 10 mL PFA, 40 min at 0.25 mL/min, 450 nm — most directly applicable (same UV-150 reactor, same wavelength, same Ir catalyst class); difference: Ni dual catalysis vs single photoredox, THF vs EtOH/buffer; adjustment: our 0.5 mL/min gives 20 min in 10 mL Stage 1, consistent with higher photon flux
